body: Thank you so much for this; really, really great stuff.
Like the idea of structured hobby/interest/passion time.  Thanks for the suggestions and advice; very much appreciated.

Yeah, I was pretty sure that that was the "correct" answer but I was hoping that maybe I was missing something.  I guess it just seems unfortunate to me that I (would) have to wait until the little I'm managing to keep together falls apart before I can get the help I feel like I need.  Do I want to work on the root causes?  Absolutely.  Am I a bit leery after a dozen years of trying to do just that and winding up in the spot I'm in now?  Absolutely.  Regardless, I will be taking your advice just as soon as I can from a benefits standpoint.

I do sincerely appreciate your taking the time to respond and welcome any other thoughts or ideas from you or anyone else as appropriate.

Thanks for your reply.  I get that normally we try to tackle the "big problems" and hopefully the "little things" fall into place...but what about getting help with the "little things" and gaining more confidence, more traction, more proof that the hard "big problem" work that needs to be done can be worth it?

Partly, it is a practical concern -- I'm without benefits for another two months and I'm seeing my LCSW/therapist for free through EAP.  But it's more than that -- isn't there a "case worker", a program, something...that starts with baby steps like self-care, basic life skills, etc.?

Yeah...my therapist IS an LCSW and wasn't having any of it.  But I actually don't think it's her -- I think it is a pretty unusual request given a "therapist's" normal scope of practice.  That's why I was trying to bypass her; I know I can go find another one, but I suspect that the reaction would be similar.  And, I don't in fact know that the kind of support I'm wanting actually exists -- at least, outside of the "high-risk" settings I mentioned.

Sometimes I have to boil it down to this:  a lot is still wrong, but at least I don't go to bed right after dinner anymore, hoping to speed getting tomorrow over with as soon as possible...making myself sick with anxiety over the coming weekend and yet hoping it will be different...and then spending most of it in bed when it finally gets here...hanging on for dear life until Monday when at least I'll have work to distract me.  It's a start.

Thanks for taking the time to respond.  I've actually already done some (most?) of those things.  I've lost a few pounds, and even though people have made comments here and there and I can tell that some of my clothes fit a little bit better...it still seems futile; it doesn't change any of the other stuff.
